question.problem:
The Taylor series for the function $f(x)$ about $x=-2$ is given by

$$
f(x)={\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }(-1)^{n+1}\frac{{3}^{n}}{n}(x+2)^{n}.
$$

Find the series expansion of ${f}^{′}(x).$

${f}^{′}(x)={\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }$
{{field-1}}$(-1)^{n+1}:(x+2)^{n-1}$
question.worked_solution:
Writing the terms of the series explicitly, we have

$$
f(x)=3(x+2)-\frac{9}{2}(x+2)^{2}+⋯+{{(-1)^{n+1}\frac{{3}^{n}}{n}(x+2)^{n}}_{⏟}}_{\text{the }n\text{th term}}+⋯.
$$

Differentiating the above series term-by-term gives

$$
{f}^{′}(x)=3-9(x+2)+⋯+{{(-1)^{n+1}{3}^{n}(x+2)^{n-1}}_{⏟}}_{\text{the }n\text{th term}}+⋯.
$$

We can now write the Taylor series for ${f}^{′}(x)$ using the sigma notation as follows:

$$
{f}^{′}(x)={\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }{3}^{n}(-1)^{n+1}(x+2)^{n-1}
$$
